children: Fortescue's unresolved talks with China's central iron-ore buying agency keeps Jefferies at neutral. "Cost headwinds, and the obvious downside risk to sales volumes and pricing for the year prevent us from turning more constructive despite the recent share price underperformance and net present value support," says analyst Mitch Ryan. Fortescue appears ready to reduce volumes in the short term to defend its long-term margins. The implication is the CMRG talks don't reflect a fair and proper market. "Time will tell who gives the most," Jefferies says. With most of the inventory build occurring in China at port, stockpiles can be run down relatively quickly if the dispute is resolved. Still, Jefferies lowers realizations to 80% for the remainder of the year to account for such a discount.  (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
